props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Callback fired when the `value` changes. Use when controlled.

props.name: className
props.description: The part's class, beside its own env-field class.

props.name: size
props.description: The height, as on every control: sm, md or lg in the current scale. Without it, the control height of the container.

Field.Description.description: Lasting guidance under the control, such as a format or a limit, linked to the control as its description.

props.name: style
props.description: Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state.

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

props.name: className
props.description: The part's class, beside its own env-field class.

Field.Error.description: A message under the control that says how to correct the value, with an error icon. It shows while the field is invalid, from its own validation or from invalid on Field.Root, and is linked to the control; match="valueMissing" and the like show it for one kind of failure, and match={true} always.

props.name: style
props.description: Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state.

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

props.name: match
props.description: Determines whether to show the error message according to the field's [ValidityState](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/ValidityState). Specifying `true` will always show the error message, and lets external libraries control the visibility.

props.name: className
props.description: The part's class, beside its own env-field class.

props.name: children
props.description: How to correct the value. Without children, the browser's validation message shows.

props.name: icon
props.description: The icon before the message, decorative, so hide an icon of your own from assistive technology, or null for none, such as for a compact error beside a control.

Field.Label.description: The field's visible name; it names the control for assistive technology.

props.name: style
props.description: Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state.

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

props.name: nativeLabel
props.description: Whether the component renders a native `<label>` element when replacing it via the `render` prop. Set to `false` if the rendered element is not a label (for example, `<div>`). This is useful to avoid inheriting label behaviors on `<button>` controls (such as `<Select.Trigger>` and `<Combobox.Trigger>`), including avoiding `:hover` on the button when hovering the label, and preventing clicks on the label from firing on the button.

props.name: className
props.description: The part's class, beside its own env-field class.

Field.Root.description: A labelled form control with its description and error, for a control envUI has no field for, such as a control of the application's own: Field.Label names Field.Control, and the description and the error describe it.

props.name: style
props.description: Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Whether the component should ignore user interaction. Takes precedence over the `disabled` prop on the `<Field.Control>` component.

props.name: name
props.description: Identifies the field when a form is submitted. Takes precedence over the `name` prop on the `<Field.Control>` component.

props.name: validate
props.type: ((value: unknown, formValues: Form.Values) => string | string[] | null | void | Promise<string | string[] | null | void>) | undefined
props.description: A function for custom validation. Return a string or an array of strings with the error message(s) if the value is invalid. Returning nothing, `null`, an empty string, or an empty array means the value is valid. Asynchronous functions are supported, but they do not prevent form submission when using `validationMode="onSubmit"`.

props.name: validationMode
props.description: Determines when the field should be validated. This takes precedence over the `validationMode` prop on `<Form>`. - `onSubmit`: triggers validation when the form is submitted, and re-validates on change after submission. - `onBlur`: triggers validation when the control loses focus. - `onChange`: triggers validation on every change to the control value.

props.name: validationDebounceTime
props.description: How long to wait between `validate` callbacks if `validationMode="onChange"` is used. Specified in milliseconds.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Whether the field is invalid. Useful when the field state is controlled by an external library.

props.name: dirty
props.description: Whether the field's value has been changed from its initial value. Useful when the field state is controlled by an external library.

props.name: touched
props.description: Whether the field has been touched. Useful when the field state is controlled by an external library.

props.name: actionsRef
props.description: A ref to imperative actions. - `validate`: Validates the field when called.

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

props.name: className
props.description: The part's class, beside its own env-field class.

Graphic.description: An application's own logo, icon or picture, from a file or an SVG component, at one of envUI's sizes: contained and centered in its box, or covering it for a photo, never stretched, and never at the file's own size.

props.name: src
props.description: The file's URL, such as an imported PNG, WebP, JPEG or SVG. While it is undefined, such as before a chosen file is read, the box stays empty at its size.

props.name: children
props.description: An SVG, such as the application's own icon component, with a viewBox.

props.name: alt
props.description: What the picture says, such as the company's name for its logo: it names the graphic as an image. `""` when the text beside it already says it, such as a logo before the name: the graphic is decorative and hidden from assistive technology.

props.name: size
props.description: The box the picture is contained and centered in: `text` 1 em, in a line of text; `icon` the icon size of the slot it sits in, such as a button's, else a control's 1 rem; `sm` 1.5 rem, `md` 2 rem, `lg` 3 rem and `xl` 5.5 rem, Avatar's sizes; `fill` a block of its container's width, and of its height where the container has a definite one. Its size never comes from the file.

props.name: aspect
props.description: The box's shape as a ratio of width to height, such as `"16/9"` or `1.5`, for a photo, a screenshot or a thumbnail: a step's size is then its height, and a fill takes its height from its width, so it needs no height from its container. Without it the box is square, or a fill the container's box.

props.name: fit
props.description: `contain` shows the whole picture inside the box; `cover` fills the box and crops what overflows, for a photo or a screenshot. It applies to a file; an SVG component is contained.

props.name: tint
props.description: `own` keeps the picture's colors; `text` paints a one-color picture in the text color, so it follows the theme and the state of the control it sits in. A file in the text color is drawn through a CSS mask, which needs a file from another origin to be served with CORS.

Grid.description: Lays its direct children out in columns, `gap` apart: a number of equal columns, a template, or as many as fit at a minimum width. A CSS grid that sizes to its content and never paints.

props.name: columns
props.description: The columns: a number of equal columns, a `grid-template-columns` template, such as `'minmax(0, 2fr) minmax(0, 1fr)'`, or `{ min: '12rem' }`, as many equal columns as fit at that width or wider, with empty columns where items run out, so every item keeps one width. One column by default.

props.name: gap
props.description: The space between rows and columns, a step of the spacing scale. None by default.

props.name: align
props.description: How each child lines up in its cell's height: stretch, the default, fills the row; start, center and end keep it at its own height.

props.name: render
props.description: The element to render, for its meaning, such as render={<section />} or render={<ul />}, or another component to lay out without a wrapper, such as a Surface: the primitive's attributes merge into its props. It must forward native props and refs. A div by default.

props.name: ref
props.description: The rendered element, a div by default. Its type is the element type parameter, which a ref passed in sets: a ref to the element that render makes, such as useRef<HTMLElement>(null) with render={<section />}, type-checks.

props.name: name
props.description: A name for this node, such as "filters" or "summary", for the application's styles and tests to find it by; it renders as `data-env-name`. A component's part class names its node instead.

props.name: container
props.description: Makes the element a size container of this name, for container queries on its inline size, such as container="filters" for `@container filters (width >= 37.5rem)`. A container is as wide as its context gives it, never as its content. container="env-window" makes the element a window of its own on purpose, such as a preview frame, whose content lays out at its window class; other `env-*` names are envUI's own.

props.name: padding
props.description: The inset on every side, a step of the spacing scale. None by default.

HighlightedCodeBlock.description: Source with its syntax colored, in the code theme of the app theme, with that code theme's own colors; copy always uses the original string. The highlighter loads with the first block that names a language it knows. For a command or output, CodeBlock shows plain text without it.

props.name: language
props.description: The language to highlight: js, jsx, ts, tsx, java, json, html, xml, css, sql, sh, bash, yaml, md or ini, or their full names. Other values, and none, leave the source plain text.

props.name: children
props.description: The source, as one string; it is shown and copied as it is.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the block in its heading and for assistive technology, such as a file name, or content such as a file-type icon and a path link. Without one, the code takes the generic name of its language, such as Plain text code or TypeScript code, from messages.codeBlock.label.

props.name: headerEnd
props.description: Content at the end of the heading, before the copy button, such as Open in editor, Run, or a switch between npm, pnpm and yarn, placed as given.

props.name: copyable
props.description: Shows a copy button in the heading that copies the source; false by default.

props.name: wrap
props.description: Wraps long lines instead of scrolling them; false by default.

HoverCard.description: Supplementary details that open beside their trigger on hover and keyboard focus, like a link preview. className, style, ref and data attributes go to the card.

props.name: trigger
props.description: The element that opens the card on hover and keyboard focus; it receives the ref. Text, such as a span or Text that holds text, takes a quiet dotted underline, env-hover-detail; give it tabIndex={0}, so keyboard focus reaches it, which envUI reports while developing. A link or another control keeps its own look.

props.name: underline
props.description: Whether a text trigger takes the quiet dotted underline, env-hover-detail, that says it shows more on hover or focus. False leaves its class alone, for text styled its own way, such as

props.name: children
props.description: The details. Supplementary: never the only place essential information appears.

props.name: side
props.description: bottom, top, left or right, or inline-start and inline-end, which follow the text direction.

props.name: align
props.description: Lines the card up with the trigger's center, start or end along the side.

props.name: delay
props.description: Milliseconds the pointer rests on the trigger before the card opens; focus opens it at once.

props.name: closeDelay
props.description: Milliseconds before it closes once the pointer leaves the trigger and the card.

props.name: width
props.description: The widest the card grows: md, 20 rem, or lg, 28 rem. It is as wide as its content from 12 rem up, and narrows to fit the window.

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the card shows; with `onOpenChange` it controls the card.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether an uncontrolled card starts open.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called with the new state, and why, when hover, focus or Esc opens or closes the card.

props.name: skeleton
props.description: Shows it and its content as a busy skeleton while that loads; turning it on or off renders the content anew.

Icon.description: The SVG that envUI's symbols render: `--env-icon-size` square, the size the component around it sets, such as a List row's start, and else the control icon size; `currentColor`, and hidden from assistive technology unless labelled. An application's own icons and logos go in Graphic, as a file or an SVG component inside it.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for a meaningful standalone icon. Omit for decoration.

props.name: tone
props.description: The icon's color: a status tone's text color, `--env-color-fg-{tone}`, such as success for a step that is done, or neutral, the color of the text around it.

IconButton.description: A square button that shows its icon alone, named by aria-label or aria-labelledby, such as a close button with the Close cross; with href, a native link. Without a variant it takes its container's, and else the neutral secondary one.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: The id of visible text that names the action; this or aria-label.

props.name: disabled
props.description: A disabled button cannot be pressed; a disabled link has no destination, cannot be focused or followed, and reports aria-disabled.

props.name: href
props.description: The destination: the button is a native link, through the LinkProvider's link component.

props.name: variant
props.description: The emphasis, as Button's. Without it, the button takes the variant its container gives, such as ghost in a toolbar, and else secondary.

props.name: tone
props.description: The meaning, as Button's.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: The action's name, which assistive technology announces, such as Open settings.

props.name: icon
props.description: The icon, such as Settings.

props.name: pending
props.description: As Button's: a spinner replaces the icon while the work runs.

props.name: size
props.description: As Button's: the height, and the width, of the square button.

props.name: render
props.description: As Button's: another element to render the button as, such as a label for a file input shaped like an icon button. Its class, look, state attributes, icon and handlers merge into that element's props; disabled reports aria-disabled and blocks presses.

Kbd.description: A keyboard key, or a combination of keys with keys.

props.name: keys
props.description: Keys pressed together, such as ['Ctrl', 'P']: one key cap each, joined by the separator, inside an outer `<kbd>`. A key can be any content, such as an icon for an arrow or Return. Without it, the children are one key.

props.name: separator
props.description: What joins the keys: a +, null for none, as in ⌘⇧P, or a word for keys pressed one after another, such as then in G then I.

Link.description: A destination inside running text, underlined by default. It is a native link, through the LinkProvider's link component, in the text button's colors.

props.name: href
props.description: The destination: the element is a native link, through the LinkProvider's link component.

props.name: disabled
props.description: A disabled button cannot be pressed; a disabled link has no destination, cannot be focused or followed, and reports aria-disabled.

props.name: underline
props.description: Underline the link; true by default, so it stands out from the text around it.

LinkProvider.description: Connects envUI links to the application's router without a router dependency in envUI.

props.name: component
props.description: Renders every envUI destination (Button, Link, the destinations of NavigationBar, NavigationRail and NavigationDrawer, Card, Pager links and menu links with href). It must render an anchor and forward native props and ref, for example a router's link that navigates on the client.

props.name: children
props.description: The application, or the part of it whose destinations use the link component.

List.Item.description: One `li` row with a label, a description and content at its end, or the control of the setting it names; the current row, content at its start, and in a reorderable list a drag handle.

props.name: label
props.description: The row's name, in the row's text color, such as an item's name, or in an interactive row a link or text Button marked `data-row-target`, which then reads in the row's text color too. It takes the room the row leaves and wraps; it is never cut short. Undefined, such as over a placeholder item, a skeleton shows a bar in its place.

props.name: description
props.description: A short fact in muted text below the label, such as who changed the item and when. Given as undefined, such as over a placeholder item, a skeleton shows a bar in its place.

props.name: end
props.description: Content at the end of the row, such as a Button or a Badge, which keeps its size; it moves below the text when it doesn't fit beside it. The control of the setting a row names goes in control.

props.name: children
props.description: More content under the label and the description, such as a row of Badges, placed as given.

props.name: control
props.description: The control of the setting the row is about, at the row's end: a Switch, a Checkbox, a Radio or a field, such as a Select or a SegmentedControl, given no label of its own. The row's label names it and the row's description describes it, so it isn't labelled twice.

props.name: interactive
props.description: The row opens something through a link or button inside: it reacts to hover, keyboard focus inside it and presses. Mark that link or button `data-row-target` to stretch it over the row; the other links, buttons and fields in the row, such as an author's link in the description, stay clickable above it.

props.name: current
props.description: The current row, such as the one whose details show beside a list: the selected fill and medium text, and `aria-current="true"` on its `data-row-target` element in the label, description or children, or on the row without one.

props.name: start
props.description: Content before the label, such as an Avatar, an icon or a Checkbox for choosing several rows; a row whose checkbox is checked takes the selected fill.

props.name: textValue
props.description: The row's label as plain text, for its drag handle's name and the reorder announcements where `label` isn't a string.

props.name: skeleton
props.description: Shows it and its content as a busy skeleton while that loads; turning it on or off renders the content anew.

List.Root.description: A `ul` of rows, filled tiles joined into one block by small gaps with shared outer corners, for items people scan, open or choose. In a muted Surface that holds only lists, the rows take the raised fill, so they stand out from it. With onReorder, people move the rows by their handles. With a title, a heading above the rows names the list.

props.name: title
props.description: The heading above the rows, such as Remote access for a group of settings. It names the list, so that a page of such groups has one consistent outline.

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: The heading's level, for the page's outline: 2 under the page's own heading, 3 inside a section that has one. It looks the same at every level.

props.name: description
props.description: A sentence under the title, in muted text, such as what the group's settings change. It describes the list.

props.name: headerEnd
props.description: Content at the end of the title's line, outside the heading, such as an Add Button, a Manage link or a count, placed as given; it wraps below the title when it doesn't fit beside it.

props.name: density
props.description: How tightly the rows pack: xs, sm, md or lg changes only their block padding, never the text.

props.name: onReorder
props.description: Makes the rows reorderable: each row gets a drag handle, at its start unless handlePlacement puts it at its end, moved by dragging it, by pressing it or by keyboard, and the list calls this with the row's index and the index it is dropped at. The application moves the item in its own state; nothing moves until it does. The rows are the list's children, directly or in arrays and fragments: List.Item elements, or elements of a row component that passes the props it doesn't use on to its List.Item, such as `function SlideRow({ slide, ...props }) { return <List.Item {...props} label={slide} />; }`.

props.name: handlePlacement
props.description: Where each row's drag handle sits in a list with onReorder: at the row's start, before its start content, or at its end, after its end content and its control.

props.name: skeleton
props.description: Shows it and its content as a busy skeleton while that loads; turning it on or off renders the content anew.

Markdown.description: CommonMark prose with tables, task lists and other extensions, in envUI typography and code. The names of its table regions and task checkboxes come from EnvUIProvider's messages.markdown.

props.name: children
props.description: The Markdown string to render.

props.name: headingOffset
props.description: Add to the document's heading levels; levels are capped at h6.

props.name: renderLink
props.description: Receives safe hrefs and native anchor props. Retain a real anchor destination.

props.name: allowLinkSchemes
props.description: Schemes a link may take beside the safe ones, such as `['vscode']` for links that open the editor, or the application's own. A link keeps a relative destination or an http, https, mailto, irc, ircs or xmpp one either way; one with another scheme renders as plain text.

props.name: codeCopyable
props.description: Gives each code block a copy button; false by default.

props.name: components
props.description: react-markdown component overrides, merged over envUI's own; the application's win. Native props such as id and className reach the element.

props.name: remarkPlugins
props.description: remark plugins that run after envUI's own Markdown extensions.

props.name: rehypePlugins
props.description: rehype plugins, such as heading ids; envUI adds none of its own.

props.name: allowHtml
props.description: Keeps raw HTML in the Markdown, such as details, sub, sup or an img with a width, for trusted content such as the application's own docs or a README. Only rehype-raw in rehypePlugins renders it, so give a sanitizer with it, such as rehype-sanitize. Without it, raw HTML is dropped, apart from kbd around plain text.

Menu.CheckboxItem.description: An independent on/off option; a check mark shows while it is on.

props.name: checked
props.description: Whether the option is on, for an item the application controls; a check mark shows while it is.

props.name: defaultChecked
props.description: Whether an uncontrolled item starts on.

props.name: onCheckedChange
props.description: Called with the new state when the item is toggled.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The item stays in place, dimmed, but cannot be toggled.

props.name: closeOnClick
props.description: Close the menu after toggling; off by default, so several options can change.

props.name: className
props.description: Class of the item's row.

props.name: start
props.description: Content before the label, such as the Settings icon or an Avatar in an account switcher: an envUI icon takes the icon size and other content keeps its own, and the labels of the menu's rows still line up. It is hidden from assistive technology, since the label names the item.

props.name: children
props.description: The item's label, which names it.

props.name: textValue
props.default: children, when it is a string
props.description: The label as plain text, which typing a letter in the open menu matches, where children isn't a string, such as a label with a Badge or emphasis inside.

props.name: description
props.description: A second, muted line; announced as the item's description.

props.name: shortcut
props.description: Keyboard hint at the end, such as Ctrl+P, shown as Kbd keys and announced as aria-keyshortcuts; a sequence, such as Ctrl+K Ctrl+S, shows its keys without the attribute. The application handles the shortcut itself.

props.name: end
props.description: End content, such as a Badge or a count; it is part of the item's name.

props.name: ref
props.description: The item's row element.

Menu.Group.description: A labelled group of related items, with a small heading above its rows.

props.name: label
props.description: Small heading that names the group for assistive technology too.

props.name: children
props.description: Items of the group.

Menu.Header.description: Non-interactive context at the top of a menu, such as the signed-in account.

props.name: children
props.description: The context, such as the signed-in person's avatar, name and e-mail address.

Menu.Item.description: One action (onClick) or destination (href) in a Menu. Destinations use the LinkProvider's link and close the menu as they are followed.

props.name: tone
props.description: The item's tone: danger marks a destructive action, such as Delete, its label and icon in the danger color; its row highlights as any other's.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The item is unavailable: it stays in place, dimmed, and reports aria-disabled; its action does not run, and a destination has no link to follow.

props.name: aria-current
props.description: Marks a destination as the page shown now, such as aria-current="page" on the current one of a NavigationBar's destinations that its More menu holds.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: The item's accessible name, where its label and end content don't say it as wanted, such as Inbox, 3 new for a destination whose count shows as a badge.

props.name: className
props.description: Class of the item's row.

props.name: start
props.description: Content before the label, such as the Settings icon or an Avatar in an account switcher: an envUI icon takes the icon size and other content keeps its own, and the labels of the menu's rows still line up. It is hidden from assistive technology, since the label names the item.

props.name: children
props.description: The item's label, which names it.

props.name: textValue
props.default: children, when it is a string
props.description: The label as plain text, which typing a letter in the open menu matches, where children isn't a string, such as a label with a Badge or emphasis inside.

props.name: description
props.description: A second, muted line; announced as the item's description.

props.name: shortcut
props.description: Keyboard hint at the end, such as Ctrl+P, shown as Kbd keys and announced as aria-keyshortcuts; a sequence, such as Ctrl+K Ctrl+S, shows its keys without the attribute. The application handles the shortcut itself.

props.name: end
props.description: End content, such as a Badge or a count; it is part of the item's name.

props.name: ref
props.description: The item's row element.

props.name: rel
props.description: The destination's relationship to the page, such as noopener, as on a native link.

props.name: href
props.description: The destination: the item is a link, through the LinkProvider's link component, and the menu closes as it is followed.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Runs as the destination is followed, before the menu closes, such as to record the choice; the link still navigates.

props.name: target
props.description: Where the destination opens, such as _blank, as on a native link.

props.name: closeOnClick
props.description: Close the menu once the action runs; false keeps it open, for an action people repeat, such as Zoom in.

Menu.RadioGroup.description: One choice among several items; the checked item shows a check mark.

props.name: value
props.description: Value of the checked item, or null for none, for a group the application controls.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Value of the item an uncontrolled group starts with checked, or null for none.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called with the chosen item's value.

props.name: children
props.description: Menu.RadioItem elements.

props.name: label
props.description: Optional heading; the group is then labelled like Menu.Group.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: Id of a heading elsewhere in the menu that names the group, in place of label.

props.name: value
props.description: The value the Menu.RadioGroup reports when this item is chosen.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The item stays in place, dimmed, but cannot be chosen.

props.name: closeOnClick
props.default: true, or the closeOnClick of the ThemeMenuRadioGroup around it
props.description: Close the menu after choosing.

props.name: className
props.description: Class of the item's row.

props.name: children
props.description: The item's label, which names it.

props.name: start
props.description: Content before the label, such as the Settings icon or an Avatar in an account switcher: an envUI icon takes the icon size and other content keeps its own, and the labels of the menu's rows still line up. It is hidden from assistive technology, since the label names the item.

props.name: end
props.description: End content, such as a Badge or a count; it is part of the item's name.

props.name: textValue
props.default: children, when it is a string
props.description: The label as plain text, which typing a letter in the open menu matches, where children isn't a string, such as a label with a Badge or emphasis inside.

props.name: description
props.description: A second, muted line; announced as the item's description.

props.name: ref
props.description: The item's row element.

Menu.Root.description: A list of actions and destinations that opens from a trigger; keyboard and focus follow the menu pattern. The popup is raised above the page, with rows of the scale's row height, full-width hairline separators and small keys for shortcuts.

props.name: trigger
props.description: The control that opens the menu, such as a Button or an AvatarButton; it receives the menu button semantics and ref, so it must accept native props and a ref.

props.name: aria-label
props.default: the trigger's name, such as Account
props.description: Accessible name of the menu, where its trigger's name doesn't say it.

props.name: children
props.description: Menu.Header, Menu.Item, Menu.Group, Menu.RadioGroup, Menu.CheckboxItem, Menu.Submenu and Menu.Separator elements.

props.name: side
props.description: The side of the trigger the menu opens on; it flips to the other side where the window has no room. inline-start and inline-end follow the text direction.

props.name: align
props.description: How the menu lines up with the trigger along that side.

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the menu is open, for a controlled menu; leave it out and the menu opens and closes itself.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether an uncontrolled menu starts open.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called with the new visibility, and why, as the menu opens or closes.

props.name: className
props.description: Class of the menu popup. ref, style, data attributes and the other native props go to the popup too; the trigger is the element you pass.

props.name: skeleton
props.description: Shows it and its content as a busy skeleton while that loads; turning it on or off renders the content anew.

Menu.Submenu.description: A row that opens a nested menu beside it, on hover or with the keyboard. The submenu opens in the theme of its menu, and lines its first row up with the row that opened it.

props.name: label
props.description: The label of the row that opens the submenu, which names the row.

props.name: children
props.description: The submenu's items: Menu.Item, Menu.Group, Menu.Separator and the other parts, nested submenus too.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name of the submenu; by default the label, when it is a string.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The row stays in place, dimmed, but cannot open its submenu.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled visibility; onOpenChange also suits loading the items as the submenu opens.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether an uncontrolled submenu starts open.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called with the new visibility, and why, as the submenu opens or closes, for example to load its items.

props.name: className
props.description: Class of the submenu popup.

props.name: ref
props.description: The submenu popup's ref.

props.name: style
props.description: The submenu popup's inline style.

props.name: triggerProps
props.description: Attributes of the row that opens the submenu, such as a className, a style, a ref or a data attribute; the submenu's own className, style and ref are its popup's.

props.name: start
props.description: Content before the label, such as the Settings icon or an Avatar in an account switcher: an envUI icon takes the icon size and other content keeps its own, and the labels of the menu's rows still line up. It is hidden from assistive technology, since the label names the item.

props.name: end
props.description: End content, such as a Badge or a count; it is part of the item's name.

props.name: textValue
props.default: children, when it is a string
props.description: The label as plain text, which typing a letter in the open menu matches, where children isn't a string, such as a label with a Badge or emphasis inside.

props.name: description
props.description: A second, muted line; announced as the item's description.

Menubar.Menu.description: One menu of a Menubar.Root: a small text trigger and the menu that opens below it. After a command, focus returns to where it was before the menubar took it, as in a desktop application.

props.name: label
props.description: The trigger's text, such as File, or content such as an icon beside the text.

props.name: accessKey
props.description: A letter of the label, such as F for File. With Menubar.Root's accessKeys, holding Alt underlines it, in the label's text also beside an icon or inside an element such as a span, and Alt with the letter opens the menu.

props.name: triggerProps
props.description: Attributes of the trigger button, such as a className, a style, a ref or a data attribute; the menu's own className, style and ref are its popup's.

props.name: children
props.description: The menu's items: Menu.Item, Menu.Submenu, Menu.Separator and the other menu parts.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name of the menu; by default the label, when it is a string.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The trigger stays in place, dimmed, but doesn't open its menu.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled visibility.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether an uncontrolled menu starts open; closed by default.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called when the menu opens or closes, with the element that had focus before the menubar took it.

props.name: className
props.description: Class of the menu popup.

props.name: ref
props.description: The menu popup's ref; the trigger is the menubar's own.

props.name: style
props.description: The menu popup's inline style.

Menubar.Root.description: An application menubar: a row of small text buttons that open menus, such as File, Edit, View and Help. Once a menu is open, hovering another trigger or pressing ← and → switches to its menu. Opening a menu neither locks scrolling nor shifts the page.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name of the menubar, such as Application menu.

props.name: children
props.description: Menubar.Menu elements.

props.name: accessKeys
props.description: Desktop access keys, off by default: holding Alt underlines each menu's accessKey, Alt with that letter opens the menu, and Alt alone moves focus to the menubar and back. Turn it on for one menubar per window.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables every menu of the menubar.

Message.description: One entry of a conversation, such as a chat message or a comment, as an article: a compact bubble at the inline end for your own messages, full-width content for others', with an optional author, meta, status and actions.

props.name: from
props.description: self: written by the person using the app, a compact bubble at the inline end. other: from anyone else, such as an assistant or another participant, full-width content without a bubble.

props.name: author
props.description: Who wrote the message, such as a name, shown above it at weight 500, or content such as a link to their profile with a Bot or Owner Badge. Leave it out where the conversation makes it clear, such as on your own messages in a conversation with one person.

props.name: start
props.description: Content beside the message, at its inline start, placed as given, such as the author's Avatar or an assistant's mark, in a column of its own beside the header and the content.

props.name: meta
props.description: Supporting facts beside the author, in the muted color, such as the time or a RelativeTime.

props.name: actions
props.description: Small actions below the message, such as Copy or Try again: buttons without a variant or size of their own are small ghost buttons, at the inline end for your own messages. false and null count as absent.

props.name: status
props.description: A message on its way, sending, with a spinner and Sending; one that could not be sent, failed, with an error icon and Not sent in the danger tone and, on your own message, a red outline around the bubble; or a reply still being written, working, with a spinner and Working, such as an agent's while it runs, last in a MessageList with aria-busy. Without it the message is sent.

props.name: statusLabel
props.description: The content beside the status icon, such as "Could not deliver", a sentence with a Try again link or the step a reply is on, Running tests…. It overrides EnvUIProvider's `messages.message.sending`, `.failed` and `.working`.

props.name: children
props.description: The message. Plain text keeps its line breaks; formatted content, such as Markdown, fills the width of a message from someone else. A working message shows the reply streamed so far, or only its status while it is empty.

props.name: skeleton
props.description: Shows it and its content as a busy skeleton while that loads; turning it on or off renders the content anew.

MessageList.description: The messages of a conversation in order, as a log: assistive technology politely announces messages added anywhere in it and text that changes. While a reply is on its way or streams in, set aria-busy, so assistive technology waits for it to finish instead of announcing every step, and show it as a Message with status working, last. Set follow where the list scrolls by itself. Name it with aria-label or aria-labelledby.

props.name: follow
props.description: The list scrolls by itself and follows the conversation: it fills the height its container gives it, opens at the latest message and keeps the latest in view while the reader is at the end. Once they scroll away and more arrives, a Jump to latest button shows at its foot, which scrolls back to the end.

props.name: jumpToLatestLabel
props.description: The text of the Jump to latest button of a list that follows. It overrides EnvUIProvider's `messages.message.jumpToLatest`.

Meter.description: A measurement within a known range, such as the seats assigned of a plan or the storage used of a quota: a label, an optional value and a bar, exposed as a meter. For how much of a task is done, use Progress.

props.name: value
props.description: The measurement, between min and max. A value outside the range shows, and is reported, as the nearest end.

props.name: layout
props.description: stacked puts the label and the value on a row above the bar; inline puts the label, the bar and the value on one line, as in a table's usage column or a list row.

props.name: label
props.description: What the bar shows, such as Seats assigned; it shows with the bar and names it. Leave it out for a bare bar named with aria-label or aria-labelledby, such as by the name beside it in a row; without a label or valueText the bar has no row above it.

props.name: min
props.description: The low end of the range.

props.name: max
props.description: The high end of the range.

props.name: valueText
props.description: The value as text at the end of the label's row, formatted by the application, such as 2 of 5 or 40%. Without it, no value shows.

props.name: aria-valuetext
props.description: The value as assistive technology reads it, with its unit in words, such as 2 of 5 seats. Without it, a screen reader reads the value as a percentage of the range, in the locale of the nearest EnvUIProvider.

MonthPicker.description: A field for a month of a year that shows the value in the reader's locale and opens a year of months to choose it from, with keyboard access like Calendar's.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called with the new state, and why, when the popup opens or closes.

props.name: value
props.description: The value: a month as YYYY-MM. null, or an empty string, for none.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The value an uncontrolled field starts with, and that a form reset restores; none by default.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Receives the new value as YYYY-MM, or null once the field is cleared.

props.name: min
props.description: The earliest month, as YYYY-MM; earlier months are unavailable.

props.name: max
props.description: The latest month, as YYYY-MM; later months are unavailable.

props.name: locale
props.description: The locale of the shown value and the month names: EnvUIProvider's, else the browser's. Months are Gregorian, also in a locale with a calendar of its own.

props.name: formatOptions
props.description: How the field shows the value: Intl.DateTimeFormat options, by default the long month and the year, in the Gregorian calendar unless they name another.

props.name: clearLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the field's clear button and text of the popup's.

props.name: thisMonthLabel
props.description: The popup's shortcut to the current month.

props.name: previousYearLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the popup's previous year button.

props.name: nextYearLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the popup's next year button.

props.name: ref
props.description: The field's button, which shows the value and opens the popup.

props.name: className
props.description: The field's class, on its root element.

props.name: style
props.description: Styles of the field's root element.

props.name: name
props.description: The name the value is submitted under with a form.

props.name: required
props.description: A value is needed: an empty field keeps its form from submitting and takes focus.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: The value can be read and focused but not changed.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Shown while the field is empty and its label floats or is hidden.

props.name: clearable
props.description: A clear button in the field and in the popup removes the value.

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the popup is open; with `onOpenChange` it controls it.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether an uncontrolled popup starts open; closed by default.

props.name: popupHeader
props.description: Content at the top of the popup, above the calendar or the list, such as presets: buttons for Tomorrow or Next Monday that set the value, from a field the application controls.

props.name: popupFooter
props.description: Content in the popup's footer, after its shortcut to the current date or time and before Clear, such as a note of the time zone or another action.

props.name: label
props.description: The field's visible name, above the field, such as Project name; it also names the control for assistive technology.

props.name: description
props.description: Lasting guidance under the field, such as a format or a limit, linked to the control as its description.

props.name: error
props.description: A message under the field that says how to correct the value. While it is set, the control is invalid (aria-invalid) and the message joins its description, after the description.

props.name: size
props.description: The control height, sm, md or lg; without it, the container's, and else md.

props.name: visibleLabel
props.description: The label shows above the field. false hides it, for a field whose purpose is clear without it, such as a search in a toolbar: the label still names the field for assistive technology, and a placeholder gives the visible guidance.

NavigationBar.description: The navigation bar for compact windows, such as phones: up to five destinations side by side, each an icon above its label, at the bottom of the window. A `nav` landmark; the current destination reports aria-current="page", and every destination is a tab stop.

props.name: destinations
props.description: The application's destinations, the same array NavigationRail and NavigationDrawer take. Give the bar 3 to 5: past 5 it shows the first 4 and a More item that opens the rest in a menu. Groups and nested destinations don't show: a destination whose `children` hold the current one takes the current fill.

props.name: background
props.description: The bar's background, named as Surface's and Card's: default, the default surface color, the app frame's own fill that stands apart from the page; page, the page's background, the same as the content beside it, from which a Scaffold sets it apart with a hairline. On a surface, such as a Sheet, both take the surface's color.

props.name: visibleLabel
props.description: Whether the destinations' labels show under their icons. False shows the icons only, for an icon-only bar such as a code editor's activity bar: each label still names its destination and shows in a tooltip on hover and keyboard focus.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Names the navigation landmark, such as Main or Project; give each landmark of a page its own.

props.name: skeleton
props.description: Shows it and its content as a busy skeleton while that loads; turning it on or off renders the content anew.

NavigationDrawer.description: The navigation drawer for expanded and larger windows: a column at the window's start with every destination as a row of icon, label and count, under the headings of their groups, and nested destinations in sections that open and close. It is `--env-navigation-drawer-width` wide and never wider than its container, so it also serves as a side list of a page's sections in a narrow column. A `nav` landmark; the current destination reports aria-current="page", and every destination and section button is a tab stop. Its list scrolls where the drawer is shorter than its destinations. With `resizable`, people resize it by its end edge.

props.name: destinations
props.description: The application's destinations, the same array NavigationBar and NavigationRail take: each a row with its icon, its label and its count. A heading starts each run of destinations of one `group`. A destination with `children` is a section that opens and closes, with them under it, indented.

props.name: expanded
props.description: The open sections, for a drawer whose sections the application keeps open, such as for the next visit: each a destination with `children`, named by its `id`, else its `href`, else its label. Update it from onExpandedChange. Leave it out for the drawer to keep its own.

props.name: defaultExpanded
props.description: The sections open at first, as in `expanded`, for a drawer that keeps its own. The sections that hold the current destination open as well.

props.name: onExpandedChange
props.description: Receives the open sections, as in `expanded`, as one opens or closes, and as the current destination moves into a closed section, which opens.

props.name: header
props.description: Content above the destinations, such as the application's name or a search trigger.

props.name: footer
props.description: Content below the destinations, at the bottom of the drawer, such as the account's menu.

props.name: groupEnd
props.description: Content after a group's heading, outside it, such as an IconButton that adds a project to Projects, a Menu of the group's actions or a count. It keeps its size, and the heading gives way to it.

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: The level of the groups' headings, which assistive technology lists with the page's headings: one below the heading the drawer sits under, such as 3 in a drawer under an h2.

props.name: background
props.description: The drawer's background, named as Surface's and Card's: default, the default surface color, the app frame's own fill that stands apart from the page; page, the page's background, the same as the content beside it, from which a Scaffold sets it apart with a hairline. On a surface, such as a Sheet, both take the surface's color.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Names the navigation landmark, such as Main or Project; give each landmark of a page its own.

props.name: resizable
props.description: Lets people resize the drawer by its inner edge, the end edge: a handle there that the pointer drags and the arrow keys move, between `minWidth` and `maxWidth`, which a double click returns to `defaultWidth`. Its labels and headings keep to one line: one that doesn't fit ends in an ellipsis, a label cut short shows in full in a tooltip and a heading in its title. Leave it out of a drawer in a sheet of a narrow window.

props.name: width
props.description: The drawer's width in rem while `resizable`, for a drawer the application controls with onWidthChange, such as a width it keeps for the next visit.

props.name: defaultWidth
props.description: The width in rem a `resizable` drawer starts at until people resize it, and that a double click on the handle returns it to.

props.name: onWidthChange
props.description: Receives each new width of a `resizable` drawer, in rem: while dragging with committed false, and with committed true as a drag ends, a key moves the handle or a double click resets it. Store the committed width to keep it, and pass it back as `width`.

props.name: minWidth
props.description: The smallest width people can resize a `resizable` drawer to, in rem; it never takes more than its container.

props.name: maxWidth
props.description: The largest width of a `resizable` drawer, in rem. It never takes more than half its container, such as the Scaffold, or of the window.

props.name: resizeLabel
props.description: The resize handle's name.

props.name: skeleton
props.description: Shows it and its content as a busy skeleton while that loads; turning it on or off renders the content anew.

NavigationRail.description: The navigation rail for medium windows, such as tablets: a narrow column at the window's start with the destinations one under another, each an icon above a short label. A `nav` landmark; the current destination reports aria-current="page", and every destination is a tab stop.

props.name: destinations
props.description: The application's destinations, the same array NavigationBar and NavigationDrawer take, each an icon above a short label. Groups don't show: the destinations follow one another in the array's order. Nested destinations don't show either: a destination whose `children` hold the current one takes the current fill.

props.name: header
props.description: Content above the destinations, such as a button that opens a Sheet with the NavigationDrawer, or the main action of the page.

props.name: footer
props.description: Content at the bottom of the rail, such as the account's AvatarButton.

props.name: background
props.description: The rail's background, named as Surface's and Card's: default, the default surface color, the app frame's own fill that stands apart from the page; page, the page's background, the same as the content beside it, from which a Scaffold sets it apart with a hairline. On a surface, such as a Sheet, both take the surface's color.

props.name: visibleLabel
props.description: Whether the destinations' labels show under their icons. False shows the icons only, for an icon-only rail such as a code editor's activity bar: each label still names its destination and shows in a tooltip on hover and keyboard focus.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Names the navigation landmark, such as Main or Project; give each landmark of a page its own.

props.name: skeleton
props.description: Shows it and its content as a busy skeleton while that loads; turning it on or off renders the content anew.

Page.description: The column a page's content sits in: invisible structure that never paints, centered, as wide as `width` at most, with the page gutter at its edges and the page's header at its top. Its gutters follow the window class of the region it sits in, such as a Scaffold's body or a pane, and it is the env-page container for the content inside. It adds no landmark; put it in a Scaffold's body, or the application's own main.

props.name: width
props.description: How wide the content may grow, a readable width: sm (40 rem) for a form or a settings page, md (60 rem) for a document or a detail page, lg (76 rem) for a dashboard or a list, full for content that uses the whole width, such as a board. The column is centered in the space it has.

props.name: header
props.description: The page's heading, usually a PageHeader, at the top of the same column.

props.name: gutter
props.description: Pads the column at its inline edges with the page gutter, which follows the window class of the region the page sits in: 1 rem in a compact one, 1.5 rem from medium. False leaves the edges to the content, such as a page that is one full-bleed table.

props.name: name
props.description: A name for this node, such as "settings", for the application's styles and tests to find it by; it renders as `data-env-name`.

props.name: render
props.description: The element to render, for its meaning, such as render={<article />}; a div by default. The page's class and attributes merge into its props.

props.name: children
props.description: The page's content, under its header.

PageHeader.description: The heading of a page: its title with an optional trail above it, a description, leading content, meta beside the title, actions at the end and a toolbar row under it, built from Row and Column. It responds to its own width, and can stick to the top of the area that scrolls.

props.name: title
props.description: The page's title. It wraps, balanced across its lines, and is never cut short.

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: The title's heading level: 1 for the page's own heading, a lower level for a header inside a pane or a section that sits under another heading. It looks the same at every level.

props.name: description
props.description: Under the title, such as a sentence on what the page is for, or a status line. Text takes the smaller muted text; any content, block content too, keeps its own look.

props.name: breadcrumbs
props.description: The trail to the page, usually Breadcrumbs with wrap={false}, above the title.

props.name: start
props.description: Before the title: an Avatar, an icon or a back IconButton.

props.name: meta
props.description: Beside the title, wrapping with it: Badges, such as a status, or a count.

props.name: actions
props.description: The page's actions, at the end of the title row: its primary action last. Below 37.5 rem of the header's own width, a compact one, they move under the title and wrap.

props.name: toolbar
props.description: A second row under the title: search, filters and view switches, laid out with `<Row wrap justify="between">`; see Toolbar's layouts.

props.name: sticky
props.description: Keeps the header in view at the top of the area that scrolls, over the content that scrolls under it: under a Scaffold's top bar where the document scrolls, or at the top of a Scaffold's body that scrolls. As a Page's header, what scrolls into view below it, such as a field taking focus, keeps clear of it: the header measures its height, which CSS reckons from its rows until script runs.

props.name: controlSize
props.description: The size of the buttons and icon buttons in `actions` and `toolbar` that set none: sm for a dense page, such as one in a small window, or md. Give fields in the toolbar the same `size`.

props.name: focusOnNavigation
props.description: In a Scaffold, moves focus to the title of a level 1 header when the page changes: as a new page's header mounts after the Scaffold first showed, not as a title changes. People using a screen reader then hear the new page, and the next Tab starts from it. Focus moved there shows no ring, and focus in a field or an open overlay stays where it is. False leaves focus to the application.

props.name: children
props.description: More rows under the toolbar, placed as given, such as a progress strip or an inline Alert. They stay in the header, so they stick with it.

Pager.Next.description: The destination after this one: a native link with rel="next", its title under the label Up next (EnvUIProvider's messages.pager.next), and an optional icon after them. It also stands alone, outside Pager.Root.

props.name: href
props.description: The destination; the link renders through the LinkProvider's link component.

props.name: children
props.description: The destination's title, such as the name of the next page. It shows below the direction label, wraps between words, and names the link after the label.

props.name: icon
props.description: A decorative icon, such as ArrowBack, before the previous destination's text, or such as ArrowForward, after the next one's; none by default.

props.name: rel
props.description: The link's relation to this page.

props.name: label
props.default: 'Previous' or 'Up next', or EnvUIProvider's messages.pager.previous or next
props.description: The direction label above the title, such as Previous chapter or Back to setup, for this link alone; null leaves it out.

Pager.Previous.description: The destination before this one: a native link with rel="prev", its title under the label Previous (EnvUIProvider's messages.pager.previous), and an optional icon before them. It also stands alone, outside Pager.Root.

props.name: href
props.description: The destination; the link renders through the LinkProvider's link component.

props.name: children
props.description: The destination's title, such as the name of the next page. It shows below the direction label, wraps between words, and names the link after the label.

props.name: icon
props.description: A decorative icon, such as ArrowBack, before the previous destination's text, or such as ArrowForward, after the next one's; none by default.

props.name: rel
props.description: The link's relation to this page.

props.name: label
props.default: 'Previous' or 'Up next', or EnvUIProvider's messages.pager.previous or next
props.description: The direction label above the title, such as Previous chapter or Back to setup, for this link alone; null leaves it out.

Pager.Root.description: A centered pair of previous and next destinations in a navigation landmark, its Pager.Previous and Pager.Next children; either one can be left out, and without any it renders nothing. Where the two don't fit side by side, they stack as rows of the pager's width, the previous first.

props.name: children
props.description: Pager.Previous and Pager.Next, in that order; leave one out on the first or the last page of a sequence.

props.name: aria-label
props.default: 'Previous and next content', or EnvUIProvider's messages.pager.label
props.description: The navigation landmark's name; give each pager its own where a page has several.

Pagination.description: Compact pagination for toolbars: the range of items shown, such as 1–60 of 245, and icon buttons for the previous and next pages, in a navigation landmark. The application loads the pages; the range is announced as it changes, and focus stays on the button pressed.

props.name: page
props.description: The page shown, counted from 1. It is kept within the pages that exist, so a page beyond the end shows the last one.

props.name: pageSize
props.description: The most items a page shows, such as 60; at least 1.

props.name: total
props.description: All items, when known; the range then ends with it, as in 1–60 of 245, and the last page ends the list. Leave it out for a list read in batches, where hasNextPage says when it ends.

props.name: hasNextPage
props.description: Whether a later page exists, for a list without total, such as from a cursor's has more.

props.name: pending
props.description: A page is loading: the button pressed shows a spinner, also when the load starts in an effect after the page changes, and both buttons ignore presses while staying focusable. A load for another reason, such as a refresh, makes both wait without a spinner.

props.name: hideWhenSinglePage
props.description: Render nothing while every item fits on one page, so neither button has anywhere to go.

props.name: renderRange
props.default: 1–60 of 245, or 61–120 without total, with numbers in the locale
props.description: Draws the range from the first and last item shown, the total, the page and the page count, for one pager; EnvUIProvider's messages.pagination.range writes it for every pager.

props.name: previousLabel
props.description: The previous button's accessible name and tooltip.

props.name: nextLabel
props.description: The next button's accessible name and tooltip.

props.name: variant
props.description: The buttons' variant, as on IconButton: quiet neutral icon buttons by default.

props.name: size
props.description: The buttons' height, as on every control: sm, md or lg in the current scale. Without it, they take the control height of the container, md unless the container sets another.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: The navigation landmark's name, such as Report pages, where a page has more than one.

props.name: onPageChange
props.description: Receives the page before or after the current one when its button is pressed. The application loads that page and passes it back as page. Give it, or pageHref, or both.

props.name: pageHref
props.description: The address of a page, such as `?page=3`, for a list whose pages have their own URLs: the previous and next controls are then links, through the LinkProvider's link component, which open in a new tab, are crawlable and work before hydration. A control with no page to go to reports aria-disabled and has no destination.

Panes.Pane.description: One pane: the first or the last child of Panes.Root, with an optional header.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the pane, which makes it a region landmark that people can jump to, such as Messages. Name the panes of a page's main layout; leave small panes unnamed.

props.name: header
props.description: The top of the pane, which stays in view while the pane's content scrolls under it, such as a PageHeader or a Toolbar.

Panes.ResizeHandle.description: The ResizeHandle between the panes, which resizes the sized pane: invisible on the seam with its grip of three dots, a line along it under the pointer, while dragged and with keyboard focus. Its hit area reaches only into the pane after it, so the scrollbar and the controls at the edge of the pane before it stay reachable. The arrow keys move it 1 rem a step, 5 with Shift, and a double click returns the pane to its default width. It hides while the panes stack.

props.name: label
props.description: The handle's name, which says what it resizes, such as Resize the project list.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Leaves the size as it is and takes the handle out of the tab order; a drag in progress ends without a change, as when the handle goes while it is dragged.

props.name: grip
props.description: Shows a grip of three dots at the handle's middle. false leaves the handle invisible until the pointer is over it, it has keyboard focus or it is dragged.

Panes.Root.description: A region split into two panes side by side, such as a list and its detail: one pane has a width of its own, which a Panes.ResizeHandle between them resizes, and the other takes the rest. Each pane's content scrolls on its own under its header when Panes has a height. With `stackBelow` the panes stack in a narrow region. A pane the application renders alone, such as the list while no item is open, fills the region and the handle hides. Panes fill their region with square corners; an application rounds them with its own class, and the panes follow, since the root clips them.

props.name: sized
props.description: Which pane has a width of its own, which Panes.ResizeHandle resizes: the first, such as a list or a sidebar, or the last, such as details. The other pane takes the rest of the room.

props.name: stackBelow
props.description: The window class of the Panes' own width below which the panes stack, the first above the last, each half the height, and the resize handle hides: medium (37.5 rem), expanded (52.5 rem) or large (75 rem). CSS decides it, so the server's markup is right before any script runs. Without it the panes always sit side by side.

props.name: width
props.description: The sized pane's width in rem, for Panes the application controls with onWidthChange.

props.name: defaultWidth
props.description: The sized pane's width in rem until people choose one with Panes.ResizeHandle, and the width a double click on the handle returns it to. To keep the width people choose, store what onWidthChange receives and pass it back here.

props.name: onWidthChange
props.description: Receives each new width of the sized pane, in rem: while dragging the handle with committed false, and with committed true as a drag ends, a key moves it or a double click resets it.

props.name: minWidth
props.description: The sized pane's smallest width, in rem.

props.name: maxWidth
props.description: The sized pane's largest width, in rem. It never leaves the other pane less than 16 rem.

props.name: name
props.description: A name for this node, such as "inbox", for the application's styles and tests to find it by; it renders as `data-env-name`.

props.name: children
props.description: The two panes, with a Panes.ResizeHandle between them for people to resize them.

Popover.description: A floating panel beside its trigger, for details or a small form: it opens on press, moves focus into itself, and closes with Esc, a press outside or when focus leaves it. className, style, ref and data attributes go to the popover's surface.

props.name: trigger
props.description: The control that opens and closes the popover, such as a Button or an IconButton. It must take a ref and props: it receives the press handler, aria-haspopup and aria-expanded. Leave it out for a popover the application opens with open, beside its anchor.

props.name: anchor
props.description: What the popover opens beside where that isn't its trigger, such as a table cell, a word in the text or a range of selected text: an element, its ref, or a virtual element with a getBoundingClientRect.

props.name: title
props.description: A heading at the top, such as the name of what the popover describes; it names the popover.

props.name: children
props.description: The popover's content, or a function that receives close, for an action inside it that should close the popover once it is done, such as a form's submit.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: The popover's accessible name when it has no title, such as Rename document.

props.name: side
props.description: The side of the trigger the popover opens on: top, bottom, left, right, or inline-start and inline-end, which follow the text direction. It flips to the other side without room.

props.name: align
props.description: How the popover lines up with the trigger along that side: its start, center or end.

props.name: open
props.description: Whether a controlled popover is open; update it from onOpenChange.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether an uncontrolled popover starts open.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Receives the requested state, and why, each time the popover asks to open or close: from the trigger, Esc, a press outside, focus leaving it or close (`close-press`).

props.name: width
props.description: The widest the popover grows: md, 20 rem, for details and a field or two; lg, 28 rem, for a longer form. It is as wide as its content from 12 rem up, and narrows to fit the window.

props.name: skeleton
props.description: Shows it and its content as a busy skeleton while that loads; turning it on or off renders the content anew.

PortalContainer.description: Renders envUI's overlays inside it, popups, dialogs, sheets and toasts, into another element than the document's body, and with `contained`, as part of that element.

props.name: container
props.description: The element that envUI's popups, dialogs, sheets and toasts inside render into, in place of the document's body, such as an element in a shadow root or in an iframe's document. Pass null while the element mounts: overlays wait for it.

props.name: contained
props.description: Whether the overlays belong to the container rather than the window, as in a preview of an interface: a modal one neither locks the page's scroll, traps focus nor hides the rest of the page; a dialog takes no focus as it opens; a popup opens on its own side without flipping and sizes to its content; toasts are shown without the page's F6 shortcut; and a press or Esc outside the container and the overlay's trigger doesn't close them, while the trigger and the overlay's own controls do. Make the container a containing block, such as with `contain: layout`, to keep fixed overlays, such as dialogs and their backdrops, inside it, and give it or an ancestor `container-type: inline-size`: a popup is at most as wide as that size container, or else as the window. A ContextMenu opens there too, at the pointer or below the focused element, without hiding the page or locking its scroll; a long press doesn't open it.

props.name: children
props.description: The content whose popups, dialogs and toasts render in the container.

Progress.description: How much of a task is done, such as an upload or an import: a label, an optional value and a bar, exposed as a progress bar. Pass value null while the amount of work is unknown, and the bar sweeps instead.

props.name: value
props.description: How much of the task is done, between min and max, such as 40 of 100; null while the amount of work is unknown, which shows an indeterminate bar announced as Loading.

props.name: segments
props.description: Splits the track into this many equal steps, such as 4 for a task of four stages, each filling in turn. Without it, the track is one bar.

props.name: label
props.description: What the bar shows, such as Seats assigned; it shows with the bar and names it. Leave it out for a bare bar named with aria-label or aria-labelledby, such as by the name beside it in a row; without a label or valueText the bar has no row above it.

props.name: min
props.description: The low end of the range.

props.name: max
props.description: The high end of the range.

props.name: valueText
props.description: The value as text at the end of the label's row, formatted by the application, such as 2 of 5 or 40%. Without it, no value shows.

props.name: aria-valuetext
props.description: The value as assistive technology reads it, with its unit in words, such as 2 of 5 seats. Without it, a screen reader reads the value as a percentage of the range, in the locale of the nearest EnvUIProvider.

Radio.description: One option of a RadioGroup: a native radio input with its label, and an optional description.

props.name: ref
props.description: The native radio input, so that a form library can register it and focus it; the other native props reach it too.

props.name: className
props.description: The option's class, on its root element, the label around the radio and the text.

props.name: style
props.description: Styles of the root element.

props.name: value
props.description: The value the group reports and a form submits when this option is chosen.

props.name: label
props.description: The option's visible name, such as Private; pressing it chooses the option. Without it, a List.Item whose control it is names it, such as a plan's row with its price and features, or name it with aria-label or aria-labelledby, such as a radio in a table's cell.

props.name: description
props.description: A short, muted line under the label that helps people choose, such as Only the people you invite. It is part of the option's label, so it is read with its name.

props.name: labelPlacement
props.description: Where the label sits beside the radio: end, after it, or start, before it, such as in an inline row whose label leads; the native label still names the radio.

RadioGroup.description: A set of up to five options to choose exactly one from, all in view: a native fieldset whose legend names the group, with its Radio options one under the other, or side by side.

props.name: ref
props.description: The group's fieldset.

props.name: label
props.description: The group's visible name, such as Visibility, as the fieldset's legend above the options. It names the group for assistive technology. Without it, a List.Item whose control it is names it, or name it with aria-label or aria-labelledby.

props.name: value
props.description: The value of the chosen option in a controlled group, or null for none; update it from onValueChange.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The value of the option an uncontrolled group starts with; a native form reset returns to it. Without value or defaultValue, no option is chosen until people choose one.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Receives the value of the option people choose.

props.name: description
props.description: Lasting guidance under the options, such as what the choice changes, linked to the group as its description.

props.name: error
props.description: A message under the options that says how to correct the choice, such as for a required group left empty; it joins the group's description, after the description.

props.name: name
props.description: The name every radio of the group submits its value under. Set it in a form; without it the group takes a unique generated name, so its radios still work as one group.

props.name: required
props.description: Require a choice before the form submits, through native constraint validation.

props.name: orientation
props.description: How the options are laid out: vertical, one radio under the other, each before its label with its description under the label; or horizontal, side by side, wrapping onto more lines, for two or three short options.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disable every option of the group; a disabled group can't be focused or changed.

RelativeTime.description: A moment in a time element as text relative to now, such as "3 hours ago", with the date and time in a tooltip. One shared clock keeps every RelativeTime on the page current.

props.name: value
props.description: The moment to describe: a Date, milliseconds since 1970 or a date string such as an ISO 8601 timestamp. An invalid moment renders nothing.

props.name: now
props.description: A fixed moment to compare with, for tests and server rendering; the text then stays as it is. Without it, or with an invalid one, the text follows the current time.

props.name: tooltip
props.description: Show the date and time in a tooltip on hover, such as "Oct 14, 2026, 9:41 AM", in the reader's time zone and the locale. Turn it off where the exact moment shows nearby. Inside an application's own Tooltip, that one describes the time instead.

props.name: renderTooltip
props.description: The tooltip's content from the moment, such as the time with its time zone, in UTC, or "Edited by Alex Morgan at 9:41"; the date and time in the locale by default.

props.name: locale
props.default: EnvUIProvider's locale for RelativeTime, else the runtime's language: the browser's, or the server's while rendering there
props.description: The language of the text, and of the date and time in RelativeTime's tooltip, as a BCP 47 tag such as "en-GB" or "de", or a list of them in order of preference.

props.name: format
props.description: How long the words are, from Intl.RelativeTimeFormat: long "3 hours ago", short "3 hr. ago" or narrow "3h ago", in the locale's own wording.

props.name: nowLabel
props.default: 'just now' or 'now' in English, the locale's word for now elsewhere
props.description: Text for a moment less than 45 seconds away, past or coming, such as "moments ago". English says "just now" of a past moment and "now" of a coming one; other languages the locale's word. RelativeTime takes EnvUIProvider's `messages.relativeTime.now` without it.

ResizeHandle.description: A handle that resizes what is beside it, such as two panes or a panel's edge: a focusable separator, named by its label, that the pointer drags and the arrow keys, Page Up, Page Down, Home and End move, with aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax and aria-valuetext. Its track is invisible, with a grip of three dots at its middle; a 1 px line shows along it under the pointer and while it is dragged, and a 2 px line in the focus color with keyboard focus. The handle's box is what the pointer reaches: place and size it with a class on the edge it moves. The application keeps the size; give the handle `aria-controls` with the id of what it resizes.
